exact_somali: Ceesawna wuu ku soo orday inuu ka hor tago isaga, wuuna isku duubay, oo qoortiisuu dhab yidhi, wuuna dhunkaday, wayna ooyeen.
attested_fact: The sentence moves through masculine-singular Ceesaw continuations with wuu/wuuna and then uses wayna ooyeen, where the discourse subject is plural.
linguistic_interpretation: The change from a nearest reviewed masculine-singular statement clitic to wayna is not automatically an agreement error; it is evidence that subject continuity cannot be assumed and discourse context is required.
project_rule_relevance: The current connective statement analyzer encodes the right clitic person set but explicitly says antecedent identity is not inferred. QA should preserve that uncertainty as a subject-continuity signal rather than silently treating the connective as a plain same-subject continuation.
test_expectation: The exact wayna connective remains recognized. Its nearest reviewed left statement subject person set is disjoint, so same_subject_continuity_agrees should be false/context-required even if right-predicate morphology is unreviewed.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Context-required benchmark item distinguishing local connective recognition from discourse-level subject identity.
proves: An attested Somali connective statement can switch from a preceding masculine-singular subject to a plural subject at wayna.
does_not_prove: It does not make every wuu-to-wayna transition grammatical, establish the morphology of ooyeen, or identify antecedents without context.

exact_somali: Dhulku wuu baroortaa, wuuna qallalaa, dunidu way daashaa, wayna qallashaa, oo dadka sarena way daalaan.
attested_fact: Dhulku wuu baroortaa is followed by wuuna qallalaa with the same masculine-singular discourse subject.
linguistic_interpretation: Positive control showing that matching nearest-left and connective subject person sets are compatible with same-subject continuation.
project_rule_relevance: A continuity signal should distinguish compatible same-subject continuation from the context-required switch in QA-CONNSTAT-CONT-001.
test_expectation: The wuuna connective remains recognized and nearest-left/right person sets overlap, so same_subject_continuity_agrees should be true independently of whether qallalaa has reviewed finite morphology.
proves: An attested same-subject wuu ... wuuna continuation.
does_not_prove: It does not mean every matching clitic pair necessarily corefer in arbitrary discourse.

exact_somali: Cali wuu yimid, wayna cuntay muus.
attested_fact: Not a corpus attestation; this is a QA minimal pair using already-reviewed statement clitics and finite surfaces.
linguistic_interpretation: A masculine-singular left subject followed by a feminine/plural connective can be grammatical only with an intentional subject switch; the checker must not call it a plain same-subject continuation.
project_rule_relevance: Tests context-required safety separately from local right-clitic/verb compatibility.
test_expectation: Local wayna + cuntay agreement may be compatible with 3sg feminine, but continuity with left wuu is disjoint and must be surfaced as context-required rather than globally supported.
training_evaluation_usefulness: Adversarial minimal pair for discourse-aware grammar evaluation.
proves: Nothing about corpus frequency; it tests project behavior using reviewed components.
does_not_prove: It does not assert a specific antecedent for wayna or that the sentence is correct without context.
